chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not befitting for the Muslim man to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman when he can find a Muslim woman, whether she is free or a slave girl.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim man to marry a Jewish or Christian woman if he can find a Muslim woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between the permissibility (ibahah) and preferability (istihbab) of marrying women of the Book, emphasizing that while valid, such unions are suboptimal when a Muslim woman is available. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the restriction is not absolute but rather a recommendation to preserve religious integrity and social cohesion within the Muslim community. The ruling underscores the priority of marital compatibility in faith, a key principle in Shia family law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not befitting for the Muslim man that he marries a Jewish woman or a Chrsitian woman when he can find a Muslim woman, whether she is free or a slave girl’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not proper for a Muslim to marry a Jewish or a Christian woman if he can find a free Muslim woman or a slave-girl.’”
